summary: Greg and his friend Maya discuss how automated suspicion and government scrutiny affect people, and Maya offers to 'googleclean' him, a fix she built. Greg, who has been surfing at home after returning from Mexico, notices that his Google text ads and search results differ depending on whether he is logged in. Comparing logged-in and logged-out searches, he finds the results strikingly different, such as a 'democratic primary' search showing anti-Hillary rants when logged in versus DNC volunteering pages when logged out.
one_line: Greg notices his personalized Google search results diverge sharply when logged in, after his friend Maya offers to 'googlecleaner' him.
key_facts: Maya tells Greg that once DHS agents fired all non-native-born Americans, the DHS got fatter and stupider.
Maya says she can 'googleclean' Greg and admits she built the googlecleaner.
Maya describes her googlecleaner as making her life borrowed time, awaiting discovery by the DHS.
Greg recalls questioning at the airport, a search, and a bootprint on his shirt.
Greg says 'Do it' when Maya offers to googleclean him.
Google text ads that Greg's blocker missed include Intelligent Design Facts, Online Seminary Degree, Terror Free Tomorrow, Porn Blocker Software, and Homosexuality and Satan.
Greg earlier noticed an Ann Coulter ringtone ad that made it past his eyes into his brain.
After returning from Mexico, Greg spent two weeks at home surfing and his pre-Mexico belly was reemerging.
Greg searched for a holistic restaurant and the search engine asked if he meant 'Hungarian Restaurants'.
Greg printed out pages from his search history and then logged out of his Google account to rerun the same searches.
A search for 'democratic primary' pointed to anti-Hillary rants on angry blogs when Greg was logged in.
When logged out, the 'democratic primary' search pointed to information on volunteering for the DNC.
Maya warns that automated suspicion of anyone matching a statistical picture of a bad guy is a dangerous trend.
